The paper focuses on transient electromagnetic scattering from a three-dimensional polyhedral cavity embedded in an infinite ground plane.
The Newmark time-stepping scheme is used for temporal discretization.
Edge elements (Nédélec elements) are used for spatial discretization.
The problem is reduced to a bounded domain by coupling the interior and exterior fields through an exact boundary condition on the cavity aperture.
The non-local boundary operator P is derived from Green's functions and couples the fields inside and outside the cavity.
Existence and uniqueness of the discrete solution are proved using Babuška–Brezzi theory.
Stability of the Newmark scheme is established.
Finite element error estimates are provided for the discrete solution.
The variational space V consists of functions in H(curl;Ω) with n̂×v = 0 on the cavity walls S.
The Hodge decomposition is used to split the solution space into subspaces.
The cavity is assumed to be a bounded, Lipschitz, polyhedral domain.
The relative permittivity is piecewise constant and sufficiently smooth.
The error estimate is derived using the Babuška–Brezzi condition and interpolation estimates for edge elements.
The Green's function is used to express the scattered field in the exterior region in terms of the field on the cavity aperture.
The coercivity of the bilinear forms aˆ1 and aˆ2 ensures the well-posedness of the variational problem.
The paper provides a rigorous numerical analysis of a finite element method for transient electromagnetic scattering in a cavity.
The results are important for applications in radar cross-section analysis and electromagnetic compatibility.
The method is suitable for simulating transient electromagnetic scattering from cavities with complex geometries.
The approach can handle non-homogeneous scatterers.
The paper establishes the convergence properties of the fully discrete problem.
The stability analysis is presented for the time-marching scheme.
The paper is concluded with a summary of the main results and their implications.
The work is based on previous studies of time-domain Maxwell's equations for scattering by bounded PEC bodies.
The method is applicable to both bounded and unbounded domains.
The paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the finite element method for electromagnetic scattering problems.
